# LUZ

> Install LUZ, find a component and copy its markup, or look up a token, a page pattern or an HTML element. MIT licence. In beta: any release may break anything, and the changelog says how to migrate.

Packages, in load order: @luz-ds/tokens, @luz-ds/core, @luz-ds/site, then one for your kind of site (@luz-ds/landing, @luz-ds/cms, @luz-ds/app or @luz-ds/docs). Use only the classes listed in each package's classes.json. After you write HTML or CSS, run `npx @luz-ds/check` on the files and fix what it reports; it reads source, so it does not replace testing in a browser.

## Get started
- [Install LUZ](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/get-started/): Pick a level, then copy one install command or the CDN tags. Each level needs the ones below it and nothing above.
- [Choose your snippet](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/get-started/snippet/): Pick what you are building and how you load it, then copy the lines. The CDN lines carry integrity hashes computed from the published files.
- [How LUZ is organised](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/get-started/structure/): Packages that depend in one direction, CSS in cascade layers inside one called luz, and one optional script.
- [How to read LUZ](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/get-started/how-to-read/): What the names in LUZ's CSS, markup and tokens tell you, and which of them you can rely on.
- [Make it yours](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/get-started/make-it-yours/): Change the colours, fonts, sizes, corners and shadows of LUZ with tokens, and adjust one component with CSS of your own.
- [With a bundler or framework](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/get-started/bundler/): Import LUZ's CSS and script in Astro or any tool that resolves package names, and keep the layer order and the fonts.
- [JavaScript modules](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/get-started/javascript/): What each optional script adds, how to load only the one you need, and what a page does without them.
- [Cascade layers](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/get-started/layers/): How LUZ sits in your cascade: one layer called luz, the order to declare, and how to override it with no !important.
- [Print styles](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/get-started/print/): What LUZ changes on paper, and how to keep or change any of it, with one layer and no extra file when you load luz.css.
- [Working with AI](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/get-started/ai/): What an AI coding agent can read, how to check what it wrote, and the accessibility reviewer you can give it.
- [Classless styles](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/get-started/classless/): The look of a button, a text field, a select and a table, and the space between paragraphs, headings and lists, on the bare element, inside one element you mark, for markup you cannot add classes to.
- [How LUZ is built](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/get-started/how-luz-is-built/): Three promises behind every release: it is made for people first and readable by AI agents, every change starts with a failing test, and nothing runs in your page that you did not load.

## Tokens
- [Tokens](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/tokens/): CSS custom properties for every colour, space, size and type value. Use the semantic ones: they change with the color mode.
- [Color](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/tokens/color/): Every colour a component may use, named by its job, with its value in light, dark and high contrast side by side.
- [Spacing and sizing](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/tokens/spacing/): The space scale for gaps and padding, and the heights of buttons and fields.
- [Typography](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/tokens/typography/): The three font stacks, the type scale in rem, and the smallest size each kind of text may use.
- [Color modes and themes](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/tokens/modes/): Switch between light, dark and high contrast with one attribute, or make a look of your own.
- [Radius](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/tokens/radius/): The corner radius scale: square, 2px, 4px at most, and round.
- [Shadows](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/tokens/shadows/): The elevation scale: how far a surface seems to float above the page.
- [Motion](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/tokens/motion/): The durations and easings of every transition, which drop to zero when the reader asks for reduced motion. Ships with @luz-ds/core.
- [Layers](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/tokens/layers/): Which layer sits on top: the z-index of every overlay, in order. Ships with @luz-ds/core.
- [Layout and breakpoints](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/tokens/layout/): How wide content gets, and where the layout changes. Ships with @luz-ds/core.
- [Color palette](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/tokens/palette/): The primitive colour scales. For theme authors only: components never use them.
- [Tokens in Figma](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/tokens/figma/): The tokens as one design-tokens file for Figma variables and other design tools, with the same names and the three modes.
- [Contrast check](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/tokens/contrast/): Check your own color overrides against the contrast LUZ promises, with one command or in the page, before they reach a user.
- [Make your own theme](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/tokens/themes/): LUZ ships one look in three color modes. A theme of your own is a file of semantic tokens: start from the template, check it, load it.

## HTML elements
- [HTML elements](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/html/): How LUZ styles each of the 116 current HTML elements, with a live example and the markup to copy.
- [Forms](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/html/forms/): Controls and the structure around them. Fields, selects and buttons get their look from a .luz-* class; textarea, output, meter and progress are styled with no class.
- [Text blocks](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/html/text/): Hold the reading content of a page: paragraphs, lists, quotations and preformatted text.
- [Inline text](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/html/inline/): Mark up words and phrases inside a block: emphasis, abbreviations, code, time, notes. Pick the element for its meaning; the style follows.
- [Page structure](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/html/structure/): Build the big blocks of a page: landmarks, headings and the sections between them. They look like plain boxes; their value is what they tell assistive technology.
- [Tables](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/html/tables/): Show data in rows and columns. A bare table has no LUZ style: add .luz-table, and wrap it in .luz-table-wrap so it can scroll.
- [Images and media](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/html/media/): Show images, sound and video, with their captions, or make parts of an image clickable.
- [Built-in widgets](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/html/widgets/): Open and close content, and show dialogs, with native elements and no script.
- [Frames and embeds](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/html/embeds/): Show content that comes from elsewhere: another page in a frame, a file in a viewer, an image that changes with the screen.
- [SVG and MathML](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/html/svg-mathml/): Draw graphics and write maths inside HTML. Both are part of the page and take the same tokens.
- [Script and canvas](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/html/scripting/): Draw with script, say what happens when script is off, and load the script itself.
- [Tracked edits](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/html/edits/): Show what changed in a text: what was taken out and what was put in.
- [Page metadata](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/html/metadata/): Tell browsers, search engines and scripts about the page. Readers never see these elements, so the cards show the markup only.
- [Document root](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/html/document/): The root of the page and the body that holds everything the reader sees. Shown as markup: LUZ styles both in its document layer.
- [Web Components](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/html/web-components/): Build custom elements: a template that is parsed but not shown, and a slot that shows the page's content inside a shadow tree.

## Components
- [Components](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/components/): Every core component, grouped by task, with a live example, the markup to copy and when to use it.
- [Accordion](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/components/accordion/): Shows and hides sections of content with the native details and summary elements, one at a time if you name the group.
- [Alert](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/components/alert/): Tells the reader about the page or a task: information, success, a warning or an error.
- [Avatar](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/components/avatar/): Shows who a person or a team is, with their initials or a photo, in three sizes.
- [Band](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/components/band/): Sets one block of a page on a tint that runs from edge to edge, while its content keeps the column.
- [Breadcrumb](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/components/breadcrumb/): Shows where the page sits in the site, as a trail of links to its parents.
- [Button](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/components/button/): Starts an action on the current page, such as saving, sending or opening a dialog.
- [Card](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/components/card/): Groups a few facts about one thing on a bordered surface.
- [Code](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/components/code/): Shows code inside a sentence, or in a block with syntax colours in every mode.
- [Color mode switcher](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/components/mode-switcher/): Lets readers choose light, dark or high contrast: radios that work without JavaScript, or one button that cycles.
- [Copy button](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/components/copy-button/): Copies a command or a value to the clipboard, and says it did.
- [Dropdown](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/components/dropdown/): A button that opens a short list of actions or links, anchored under it.
- [Figure](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/components/figure/): Shows an image, a chart or a diagram with a caption that says what it is.
- [Form fields](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/components/form/): Collect input with native fields, choices and pickers, each with a visible label, a hint and an error.
- [Icon grid](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/components/icon-grid/): Lets readers browse a set of icons by name and copy the SVG of each one.
- [Image](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/components/image/): Shows a picture in a frame of fixed shape, on a flat surface while it loads or when it is missing.
- [Meta line](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/components/meta/): Shows a few facts about something on one line, such as its date, its reading time and its author, with a dot between them.
- [Meter](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/components/meter/): Draws a value in a known range as a bar, next to its figure, with the native meter element.
- [Modal](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/components/modal/): Asks for a decision that must be made before the reader goes on, in a native dialog.
- [Navbar](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/components/navbar/): Puts the main links of a site in a header's row, and in a panel under it on a narrow screen.
- [Pagination](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/components/pagination/): Links to the pages of a list that goes on over several, with the current page marked.
- [Player](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/components/player/): Plays a video, a sound or a MIDI file in the page, with the same controls for all three.
- [Progress](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/components/progress/): Shows how far a task that takes time has got, with the native progress element.
- [Prose](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/components/prose/): Sets long text in lines of about 70 characters, with space between its blocks, whatever markup an editor writes inside.
- [Select](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/components/select/): A native drop-down list for choosing one option from a long list, with the closed box styled by tokens.
- [Sidebar](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/components/sidebar/): Holds the main navigation of a site or an app, and becomes a drawer on small screens.
- [Skip link](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/components/skip-link/): Lets keyboard users jump past the header to the main content.
- [Table](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/components/table/): Compares records across several attributes, in rows and columns that stay readable at 320 px.
- [Tabs](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/components/tabs/): Switches between panels of related content in one place; without JavaScript the panels are stacked sections.
- [Tag and badge](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/components/tag/): Labels an item with a short status or category (tag), or shows a count (badge).
- [Timeline](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/components/timeline/): Shows dated events in order, one card at a time on a rail of dates or all at once down a line; without JavaScript it is a list.
- [Toast](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/components/toast/): Confirms a small result, such as "Draft saved", without interrupting the reader.
- [Tooltip](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/components/tooltip/): Adds a short hint to a control on hover or focus; never essential content.
- [Layout objects](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/components/layout/): Lay out blocks in a stack, a row, a grid or beside an image, a group of actions, and the page itself with its sticky bar, with the o-* classes.
- [Utility classes](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/components/utilities/): Small u-* classes that do one thing each, for the cases a component does not cover.
- [Keyframes](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/components/keyframes/): Five shared animations for your own components, which stop when the reader asks for reduced motion.

## Site
- [Site](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/site/): Six self-contained components that need data of the site: search, cookie consent, color mode, language switch, submenu and banner, and how to tell whether you need them.
- [Submenu](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/site/submenu/): Groups a few links of a header under one button, so the header keeps a short row of links.
- [Banner](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/site/banner/): Tells every visitor one short thing at the top of the page, such as a sale, an event or planned maintenance.
- [Cookie consent](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/site/consent/): Asks a visitor once whether the site may use optional cookies, with Accept and Reject side by side, and remembers the answer.
- [Auto color mode](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/site/mode/): Adds an Auto choice to the color mode switcher, so the page follows the system setting or the time of day until the reader chooses a mode.
- [Language switch](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/site/lang-switch/): Lets readers go to the same page in another language, from a button in the header.
- [Search](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/site/search/): Finds a page, a section or an HTML element of a site by name, from a button in the header.
- [Class reference](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/site/classes/): Every tag and class of the site components, what element it goes on and what it does, in one place.

## Landing
- [Landing](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/landing/): What a landing page needs on top of core, from its header and hero to the blocks of an event page, and how to tell whether you need it.
- [Header](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/landing/header/): Starts every page of a landing site with its name, its main links and a few controls, in one row that stays at the top.
- [Hero](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/landing/hero/): Opens a home or landing page with its title, one sentence, the main actions and an optional picture.
- [Main and sections](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/landing/section/): Gives a landing page its rhythm: wide room between the blocks of the main, a closer one inside each section, with its head, and an optional glow behind the page.
- [Footer](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/landing/footer/): Ends every page of a landing site with who made it, its licence and a few secondary links, under a rule, in a row or as columns.
- [Stat](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/landing/stat/): Shows one figure big, with a short label under it.
- [Landing page templates](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/landing/templates/): The blocks of an event landing page to paste in and adapt, in the order a visitor reads them: hero, programme, speakers, tickets, call to action, registration and features, and a product page that puts a centred hero, a section head, stats and a footer with columns together.

## CMS
- [CMS](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/cms/): The page structure of a blog, a newspaper or any site of articles, from the header to the post listing, and how to tell whether you need it.
- [Header](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/cms/header/): Starts every page of a blog or a newspaper with the publication's name, its sections and a search: one row that stays at the top, or a masthead of three rows.
- [Page header](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/cms/page-header/): Gives a page that is not an article, such as About or Contact, its title and one sentence about what it is for.
- [Article header](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/cms/article-header/): Opens a story with its section, its title, a standfirst, who wrote it and when, and an optional lead picture.
- [Table of contents](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/cms/toc/): Lists the sections of a long article, beside the text when there is room and above it when there is not.
- [Footer](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/cms/footer/): Ends every page of a blog or a newspaper with who publishes it and a few secondary links, under a rule.
- [CMS templates](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/cms/templates/): The pieces of a blog or a newspaper that need no CSS of their own, to paste in and adapt: the content page, the article page, a post card, post listings, related posts and the author box.

## App
- [App](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/app/): The header and the dashboard of a web application, on core's shell and sidebar, and how to tell whether you need them.
- [Header](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/app/header/): The quiet bar at the top of an application's main area: the menu button, the product name on a phone, the search and the account.
- [Dashboard](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/app/dashboard/): The view of an application at a glance: its title and main action, then a grid of panels that fills the room the view has.
- [App templates](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/app/templates/): The pieces of an application that need no CSS of their own, to paste in and adapt: the app page with its sidebar, an app with no sidebar and an empty dashboard.

## Documentation
- [Documentation](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/documentation/): The shell, page head, rail, example, do and don't, pager and page foot of a documentation site, and how to tell whether you need them.
- [Shell](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/documentation/shell/): The page of a documentation site in three columns: the sidebar, the content and a rail, down to one column on a phone.
- [Page head](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/documentation/page-head/): The top of a documentation page: the eyebrow, the title, one sentence and the chips that say what the page covers.
- [Rail](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/documentation/rail/): The list of the sections of the page that stays in view beside the content, with the actions of the page under it.
- [Example](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/documentation/example/): A live preview with its code under it, in one frame, as wide as the width you give it.
- [Do and don't](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/documentation/dodont/): A Do and a Don't, one example to follow and one to avoid, each with its reason, side by side when there is room.
- [Pager](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/documentation/pager/): Two link blocks at the end of a page, to the previous page and to the next, each with the title it leads to.
- [Page foot](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/documentation/page-foot/): The small print under a page: when it was last updated, and links to edit it or report a problem.
- [Documentation templates](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/documentation/templates/): A whole documentation page to paste in and adapt, the pager of the first and the last page, and what the package does not have yet.

## Accessibility
- [Accessibility statement](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/accessibility/): LUZ aims for WCAG 2.2 level AA. What is checked on every change, what has not been tested, and the known issues. Last reviewed on 16 October 2026.

## Documentation
- [LUZ documentation](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/): Install LUZ, find a component and copy its markup, or look up a token, a page pattern or an HTML element.

## Optional
- [Full documentation for agents](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/llms-full.txt): The same pages, as text: markup, variants, when to use, keyboard.
- [Markup example: Button](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/examples/components/button.html): A page of the markup of Button, styled by LUZ; every component and pattern page has one under /examples/.
- [Classes of @luz-ds/core](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/manifests/core/classes.json): Every class, element and custom property of the package; each package has its own folder under /manifests/.
- [Elements of @luz-ds/site](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/manifests/site/custom-elements.json): The custom elements the package defines or declares, with their attributes; core has one too, in its own folder.
